subject: Stellar Media renewal: hybrid commit + usage proposal
messages:
From: Nora Lee <nora.lee@stellarmedia.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stellarmedia.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming renewal — looking to move to hybrid usage model

Hi Tessa,

We’re coming up on our April 30 renewal and the team asked me to explore alternatives to our existing fixed retainer. Over the last year Stellar’s workload patterns shifted — steady baseline usage but frequent short bursts tied to campaign launches. The fixed monthly commit is leaving us exposed during lulls and doesn’t map to expected seasonality.

We’d like to propose a hybrid structure: a smaller monthly commit + shared surge pool that we pay for when we exceed the commit. We’re also very sensitive to price increases; a 12-month price hold would be ideal.

High-level asks:
- Monthly baseline commit reduced from current 1.5M tokens -> target 1.0M tokens
- Surge pool with predictable overage rate and a first-year price hold
- One-time renewal credit to offset uplift during the transition

Can you share a proposal and whether Redwood can accommodate a 12-month price hold + a modest renewal credit? We’re open to structured incentives (multi-year step) but need predictable unit economics.

Thanks,
Nora
Nora Lee
Head of Engineering, Stellar Media
nora.lee@stellarmedia.com
[Attachment: Stellar_Current_Usage_Summary.csv (csv)]

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Nora Lee <nora.lee@stellarmedia.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — looking to move to hybrid usage model

Nora — thanks for the clear context. We can absolutely build a hybrid construct that keeps your baseline predictable while giving you headroom for spikes. Attached is a first-pass proposal (PDF) and a short summary below.

Proposal summary (first pass):
- Term: 12 months, renewal effective 2028-05-01
- Baseline commit: 1.0M tokens / month (down from 1.5M)
- Monthly price for committed tokens: $0.0009 / token (20% discount vs list for committed units)
- Surge pool (shared): 2.5M tokens available per month at $0.00145 / token (below list overage), pool capacity to be pooled and true-upped quarterly
- One-time renewal credit: $90,000 applied across first 3 invoices (prorated) to offset transition costs
- Price hold: unit pricing for committed and surge tiers held for 12 months from effective date
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation and annual true-up to reconcile committed usage vs actuals

Attachments: 20280322-Stellar-Proposal.pdf (proposal + line-item economics)

Questions we have for you:
1) Is the proposed surge pool size (2.5M/month) reasonable for peak activity?
2) Would a quarterly true-up cadence work for your finance team?
3) Any regulatory or payment term constraints we should be aware of?

I’ll loop in Vanessa and Ben on margin and contract mechanics. If you like this direction I can draft amendment language and route for signature (DocuSign).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[t] +1 415-555-0132
[Attachment: 20280322-Stellar-Proposal.pdf (pdf)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — looking to move to hybrid usage model

Tessa / Ben — quick margin read: the numbers look directionally OK but a few guardrails we should include to protect Redwood economics: 

- Limit the one-time credit to $90k max (as proposed) but cap applied only to committed invoice amounts (not overage)
- Surge pool pricing acceptable if we add a monthly carryover limit and a max burst multiplier (e.g., surge usage per month capped at 3x baseline for billing purposes)
- Add a clause to allow a renegotiation or rate adjustment if average monthly overage > 40% of committed units for two consecutive quarters
- Finance: request Net 30 by default — customers asking for Net45 should be escalated to Revenue Ops for approval

If legal is OK, I’d recommend proceeding with the proposal but flagging those three clauses.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — looking to move to hybrid usage model

Looping in commercial/legal early. A couple contract asks:

- Add a true-up exhibit with quarterly reconciliation dates and clear rounding rules (tokens rounded to nearest thousand)
- Include a Surge Pool Appendix listing how pool capacity is calculated and rollover rules (unused surge capacity does NOT rollover month-to-month)
- Add an objective metric for triggering renegotiation (Vanessa’s 40% threshold sounds fair)
- Payment terms: propose Net30; if the customer insists on Net45, we can offer Net45 in exchange for a 6% reduction in the renewal credit (i.e., $84,600 instead of $90,000)

I’ll draft the amendment text and send an editable doc to Tessa. Also recommend we prepare a short-facing one-pager for Stellar finance explaining quarterly true-ups and invoice examples.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Deal Desk | Redwood Inference

From: Nora Lee <nora.lee@stellarmedia.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stellarmedia.com
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — looking to move to hybrid usage model

Tessa — thanks, the proposal looks reasonable and aligns with our planning. A few clarifications before we sign:

1) Can you confirm the overage rate if we exceed the surge pool itself (i.e., beyond surge capacity)? We need to model worst-case bills for the campaign that starts in July.
2) Payment terms: Stellar prefers Net45, but we’re willing to accept Net30 if the renewal credit is kept at $90k. If you need to reduce the credit for Net45, let me know the delta.
3) DocuSign timeline: can you send the amendment this week? We need a signed agreement before Apr 18 to coordinate procurement and cloud finance.

If you can confirm 1) and 2) we’ll route to our legal and finance and aim to sign quickly.

Best,
Nora

On Wed, Mar 22, 2028 at 11:05 AM tessa_morgan@redwood.com wrote:
> Nora — thanks for the clear context. We can absolutely build a hybrid construct ...

[Attachment: Stellar_Current_Usage_Summary.csv (csv)]

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Nora Lee <nora.lee@stellarmedia.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — looking to move to hybrid usage model

Nora — great, glad it aligns. Answers below and next steps.

1) Overage beyond Surge Pool: If Stellar exceeds the 2.5M surge pool in a month, additional tokens will bill at $0.00195 / token (standard list overage). We’ll include a hard cap mechanism in the amendment if you want an automatic throttling trigger at your request, but by default we expect to bill overages and reconcile quarterly.

2) Payment terms: We can accept Net45, but we’d apply a small credit reduction to preserve economics per Ben’s note. To keep the full $90k credit we need Net30; Net45 reduces the credit to $84,600 (6% reduction).

Next steps:
- Ben will circulate the draft amendment with Surge Pool Appendix and True-up Exhibit by EOD today.
- I’ll upload the DocuSign envelope once the doc is ready — target send to Stellar by March 30 so legal can sign prior to Apr 18.
- I’ll also attach a short one-pager for Stellar finance showing sample invoices with quarterly true-up.

If that timeline works I’ll proceed.

Thanks,
Tessa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
